acceptance.given: An external process or aggregate reaches its configured time or output budget limit.

oracle.expected: The bounded execution reaches a deterministic unsuccessful terminal result.
forbidden: Budget exhaustion is classified as successful.
Budget exhaustion is treated as an indeterminate success or omitted outcome.
oracle.observable: A real budget-exhaustion execution is evaluated through the external-process and aggregate terminal-state path.

acceptance.then: The budget-exhausted execution has an unsuccessful terminal result.
acceptance.when: A configured execution budget is exhausted.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the authored S11 behavior selector with a process or aggregate that exhausts its configured time or output budget and observe the unsuccessful terminal outcome.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Classify a time- or output-budget-exhausted external process or aggregate as a deterministic unsuccessful terminal result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore only Toolchain execution-result handling; no Phase service state or schema changes are permitted.

slice_hint.state_transition: An external process or aggregate reaches a time or output budget limit -> The budget-exhausted execution has an unsuccessful terminal result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A budget-exhaustion run terminates deterministically as unsuccessful and is never published as successful, indeterminate success, or omitted.

acceptance.given: The compiled obligation graph contains Atomic Obligation-to-selector mappings to evaluate.

oracle.expected: Exact-cover validation reports that every Atomic Obligation has selector coverage and every selector node maps back to its covered Atomic Obligation.
forbidden: An Atomic Obligation is covered by selectors without reverse coverage.
A selector node is linked without corresponding Atomic Obligation coverage.
oracle.observable: The Exact Cover validator's graph-validation result for selector relationships, evaluated when the graph is compiled or exact-cover validation runs.

acceptance.then: The validation result establishes forward and reverse Exact Cover for every Atomic Obligation-to-selector relationship.
acceptance.when: When the obligation graph is compiled or the Exact Cover validator evaluates selector coverage.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the exact-cover negative validator against a selector mapping with an omitted reverse Atomic Obligation relation and require graph validation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate selector coverage as bidirectional Exact Cover: each Atomic Obligation maps to selector coverage and each selector maps back to its covered Atomic Obligation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persistent state or schema migration; reverting restores prior Exact Cover validation behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: unverified selector mapping -> bidirectional selector Exact Cover evaluation -> validated or deterministic violation result
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The compiled graph has no forward-only selector coverage and no selector node without reverse Atomic Obligation coverage.

acceptance.given: A fixture contains immutable historical and Failed-Candidate evidence before a Consumer or rollback transition produces new evidence.

oracle.expected: The evidence ledger retains byte-identical historical and Failed-Candidate records and creates distinct Consumer and rollback records without replacing any pre-existing record.
forbidden: A historical or Failed-Candidate record is removed, rewritten, or overwritten.
A Consumer or rollback record reuses an existing evidence record path or mutable record identity.
oracle.observable: The repository-owned replay evidence validation reports preserved prior record digests plus unique appended Consumer and rollback record identities.

acceptance.then: Evidence preservation and isolated append-only creation are accepted only after the preservation comparison and new-record uniqueness checks both pass.
acceptance.when: A Consumer or rollback transition emits evidence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Supply a Consumer or rollback evidence fixture that changes, removes, overwrites, or aliases a historical or Failed-Candidate record; require the replay evidence validator to reject the evidence set before success.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate that historical and Failed-Candidate evidence digests remain unchanged while Consumer and rollback transition evidence is create-only, uniquely identified, and isolated from existing records.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback removes only the added replay evidence-validation behavior; it must not alter historical or Failed-Candidate records, and existing evidence receipt fields remain backward-compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: Existing immutable historical and Failed-Candidate evidence -> Consumer or rollback transition emits a new isolated record -> preservation and uniqueness validation accepts or rejects the resulting evidence set.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: No pre-existing historical or Failed-Candidate evidence digest or record identity changes, and every Consumer or rollback record is a distinct newly created record; otherwise the evidence set is rejected.
